structured_output.review_summary: Static review of the supplied factory-receipt-discovery.py (1-843) and the review test script. The three prior findings are repaired, and I found no introduced defect above low severity. (1) Backfill later-page count rise: the count-drift branch (lines 333-334) now runs before the `count >= 1000` branch (335-338). Once a node has `expected_count`, a rise to >=1000 on a later page becomes a `count-drift` gap, so the retained `facts`, `page` and `expected_count` stay consistent. A node whose `expected_count` is None is always on page 1, so only a first-page observation can start a split or dense-second node, and `facts[0]['page']==1` holds. The persisted gap node satisfies the validators at 258-286 and is reset on revisit at 299. (2) Source-fetch failures: `_source_fetch_unavailable` (129-135) is an exact allow-list of the transport prefix plus four fixed messages. It is checked before the approval tokens at 178. The identity checks at 168, 172-173 and 540 are unchanged, and `run_identity` errors, the `charge()` budget errors and parse errors are not in the list, so they still raise. (3) Discovery cursor: `primary_short` is computed from the primary page only (499) and used only in discover mode (575-576). The wrapped cursor `(next_page=1, overlap_page=1, overlap_until=1)` passes `validate_checkpoint` (39-40), and `coverage_complete` stays False. No bounds changed. The residual items are low: head-revisit latency still grows with page depth during a long walk, a pre-existing blanket `except ValueError` at line 204 can relabel a budget error as `proof-unavailable`, and the new tests don't exercise some repaired paths. A pass covers only this supplied text and is not native, cadence or activation proof.

findings.title: Head revisit interval still grows with page depth during a long history walk (finding 3 only partly repaired)
findings.reason: The wrap at 575-576 only fires when the primary page is short, which is the end of listing. The overlap schedule at 486-489 is unchanged. Each overlap cycle starts with `overlap_until = page-1` and runs for about that many calls, so the next cycle starts at roughly twice the page depth. Page 1 is therefore re-read at geometrically growing intervals while `next_page` is still advancing. The unfiltered workflow listing has no 1000-result cap, because the comment at 581 says only filtered queries cap. With deep history, a new run at the head is first observed only when the overlap cursor returns to page 1. That is a delay on the order of the current page depth, i.e. hundreds to thousands of invocations. The new head test uses 3 to 5 runs, so it cannot show this. Interval coverage is not affected, because backfill adds missing watch rows and `coverage_complete` stays False. Consider bounding the overlap cycle length, for example by capping `overlap_until` or always re-reading page 1.

findings.title: Blanket ValueError around receipt_artifact/append_delivery can persist a budget failure as 'proof-unavailable'
findings.reason: This code predates the diff and is not introduced by it. The stated invariant is that budget failures must stay hard. Lines 194-205 call `receipt_artifact` and `append_delivery` through `AttemptView`, which uses the budgeted `source_api` wrapper. A `ValueError('discovery observation budget exceeded...')` or `'...API call budget reached...'` raised by `charge` or `source_read` inside that block is caught by `except ValueError` at 204. It is recorded as `reason='proof-unavailable'`, and the outcome is written at 514. If no later charge in the same invocation re-trips the budget, the checkpoint commits with a soft outcome instead of failing. The same handler also absorbs identity errors raised inside `receipt_artifact`. Re-raise budget, capacity and bound messages, or apply an allow-list like `_source_fetch_unavailable` here.

findings.title: Backfill regression does not exercise the first-page >=1000 split/dense-second path or assert the drift gap
findings.reason: The Drift source returns `total_count` 1000 only on its second workflow call, and that call is always a later page. The first-page saturation path (split, and dense-second when lo==hi) is never taken, although the printed message at line 35 says dense restart recovers. Line 33 checks only that fact pages are sequential. It does not assert that a `count-drift` gap node exists or that the manifest stack advanced. Adding both assertions would pin the repaired branch order and guard against the reorder being reverted.
